chunks: Therefore, whoever holds fast to piety, hardships are kept away from him after having drawn near, affairs become sweet for him after their bitterness, waves (of troubles) recede from him after having crowded over him, difficulties become easy for him after occurring, generosity rains fast over him after there had been famine, mercy bends over him after it had been loath, the favours (of Allah) spring forth on him after they had been dried, and blessing descends over him in showers after being scanty.
ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual and worldly benefits of Taqwa according to Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: In this passage from Nahj al-Balagha, Imam Ali (AS) articulates the metaphysical principle that taqwa acts as a divine catalyst, reversing the natural order of hardship into ease and scarcity into abundance. This concept is central to Shia spiritual psychology, where God-consciousness is not merely a state of fear but an active force that unlocks divine favor (karamat) and removes obstacles (shada'id), reflecting the promise that 'with hardship comes ease.'
